comment: How every wire of the worker protocol reads and writes JSON and base64, which Prima does with Jason and Elixir's Base on both sides of each wire (Prima.WorkerWire, Prima.WorkerAuth, Prima.Assignment, Prima.HostAPI, Prima.LocusPool, Prima.RunnerRelay, Prima.RunnerControl; none with the standard library's JSON), so a message means to the side that acts on it what it meant to the side that signed it. reads are documents (doc_b64, the bytes) each read as value: a member given twice is its first, a member of any name is a member ($serde_json::private::Number, the name serde's parser hands a number under, among them), an integer of at most max_integer_chars characters, its sign among them, is an integer kept whole, -0 is the integer 0, a fraction or an exponent is no integer, a number below a double's range reads as zero, and a zero with an exponent and no fraction reads as 0.0 whatever its sign. A read case marked go too_deep is the two ends' stated difference: Prima reads a document of any depth, and a Go reader and the runner's refuse one nested deeper than 4,096 arrays and objects before they parse it, so each side's test asserts its own answer. refused are documents no reader takes: bytes that are no UTF-8 or that spell a surrogate, an escape naming half a surrogate pair, a raw control character in a string, a member's name among them, whitespace other than space, tab, line feed and carriage return, a number past a double's range, an integer of more than 1,024 characters, and anything after the one value. writes are documents (value_json) each read and written back as bytes_b64: only quote, backslash and the control characters escaped, backspace, tab, line feed, form feed and carriage return by their two-character escapes and every other control character as \u00XX in uppercase hexadecimal, so solidus, <, >, &, U+2028, U+2029 and DEL are written as themselves, a plain map's members in the order of their names' bytes up to 32 members, an integer as its decimal digits, a float in Jason's own form. A write case marked go unwritable is one a Go writer refuses: it writes no float and no integer it did not make in Jason's spelling (minus zero), and no map of more than 32 members, which Jason writes in the order of Erlang's map of that size, by its keys' hashes, that no other writer spells; a worker service writes only values it made, and passes a document it carries on as the bytes it received. base64url are texts as Base.url_decode64/2 with padding false reads them (bytes_hex, or null for a text it refuses): unpadded or with exactly the padding it would carry, bits past the last byte ignored, nothing outside the URL alphabet and no line break; base64 are texts as Base.decode64/1 reads them, its padding required. apps/prima/test/prima/wire_json_test.exs holds Jason and Base to every case, the runner's reader (apps/locus/runner/tests/vectors.rs) is held to max_integer_chars, reads and refused, and the Go readers of the worker protocol (apps/locus/keeper/internal/wire/wirejson and macenvelope) are held to the same.

reads.why: a member given twice is its first
an object given twice is its first
a surrogate pair is one character
a fraction past a double's precision rounds
whitespace about the value and its members
a zero with an exponent reads as 0.0, its sign dropped
a zero with an exponent and no sign
a zero with a signed exponent
a zero with a fraction keeps its sign
a zero with a fraction and an exponent keeps its sign
a member named as serde's parser names a number is a member
a nested member named as serde's parser names a number
a member named as serde's parser names a number beside another
a member named as serde's parser names a number whose value is a number
a member named as serde's parser names a number, its name escaped
a document 4,097 arrays deep, which Prima reads and Go refuses unparsed
a member given twice whose second is 4,097 arrays deep: Prima keeps the first

refused.why: a high surrogate before another escape
a high surrogate at the end
a raw tab in a string
a raw line feed in a string
a raw NUL in a member's name
a raw tab in a member's name
a raw line feed in a member's name
a raw U+001F in a member's name
a raw tab in a nested member's name
a raw tab in the name of a member of an object in an array
a raw tab after an escape in a member's name
a raw tab in a member's name inside the second of a member given twice
a name that is no string

writes.why: solidus, <, >, &, U+2028, U+2029 and DEL as themselves
tab, line feed, carriage return and NUL
a plain map's members by name
a map of 32 members by name
minus zero, an integer Jason writes as 0: Go writes no number it did not make
an exponent, a float Jason writes as 100.0: Go writes no float
a fraction with a trailing zero, which Jason writes as 1.5
an exponent in capitals, which Jason writes as 1.0e5
a map of 33 members, which Jason writes in the order of Erlang's map of that size, by its keys' hashes
